subject: Urgent: FinixPay production 5xx/429 spike — mitigation & credit request
messages:
From: Katherine Liu <katherine.liu@finixpay.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, FinixPay SRE <sre@finixpay.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production errors — elevated 5xx/429 since 03:00 PST (examples attached)

Hi Sean,

We started seeing a major uptick in 5xx and 429 responses to model generation calls starting ~03:00 PST this morning after the rolling change you pushed. The error rate peaked at ~18% for our main payment flow and we've had several customer-facing timeouts. We've attached a short sample of error traces and request IDs (error-sample.log).

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether this is a model-variant routing change on your side?
- Can you apply a temporary traffic steering / fallback to the previous model variant for our production route?
- We need an estimate on how much of our SLA window was breached and an initial position on credits/refund.

This is causing outage tickets downstream — I have SRE on the thread (sre@finixpay.com). Please elevate.

Thanks,
Katherine
Katherine Liu
Head of Platform Reliability, FinixPay

Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — elevated 5xx/429 since 03:00 PST (examples attached)

Katherine — thanks for flagging and the traces. Seen and escalating internally.

Short plan:
1) We will open a mitigation runbook now and immediately route 70% of traffic for your production route to the previous model variant (roll back routing) while keeping 30% to the new variant for quick verification.
2) Dev is standing by to examine the kernel/quantization mismatch hypothesis.
3) We'll generate an incident timeline and a first-pass credit estimate after we quantify total error-time and affected tokens.

Grace (CS) and Marissa (AE), please loop procurement and confirm whether FinixPay needs an interim credit memo to unblock downstream tickets. Dev — confirm once the routing change is applied.

I will update in 30 minutes with actions taken.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Account Success — Redwood Inference

Note: we applied a temporary routing rule at 09:35 PST to shift traffic.

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — mitigation update and suspected cause

Applied mitigation: at 09:35 PST we enacted a traffic steer to previous variant (v2.1) for customer route finixpay-prod-main; current error rate dropped from 18% to ~1.2% within 6 minutes.

Preliminary root cause: during last kernel selection update, an optimization interacted poorly with 8-bit quantized weights for that specific sequence-length distribution, producing intermittent OOM-like 5xx responses under concurrency. We're rolling back the kernel selector for the affected binary and validating across our internal QA matrix.

I'll keep the rollback in place until we release a patched kernel (ETA 48 hours) unless we get direction to restore.

Dev

Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — mitigation & next steps

Thanks for the quick action — the routing change helped and customer-facing errors dropped. A couple of follow-ups:

- We saw two subsequent spikes (09:50 and 10:18 PST) that correlated with automated client retries; total lost successful requests estimated at ~6,200 over the 3-hour window.
- We need a postmortem and an exact calculation of SLA-eligible downtime/failed calls so procurement can quantify credits.
- Given impact to payments, we need an exec-level assurance this won't repeat; can you confirm whether the kernel selector change will be included in your patch release and whether you'll do a production canary before wide rollout?

Katherine

Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: credit position & exec note for FinixPay

Team — pricing/credits recommendation for FinixPay (preliminary):
- SLA baseline: 99.95% monthly availability per contract (Standard Enterprise).
- Impact window: ~03:00–06:00 PST on Nov 3. We estimate ~3.1 hours where elevated errors materially affected throughput.
- Preliminary unit economics shows ~6,200 failed calls; at their average call weight this equates to ~$9,000 in incremental spend that failed to complete.

Suggested credit options to offer (pick one quickly for outreach):
A) Service credit equal to 50% of the failed-call value (~$4,500) plus 1 month of priority support at no charge;
B) Full failed-call reimbursement (~$9,000) conditioned on acceptance of a 90-day production canary for kernel updates;
C) 5% invoice credit for the billing month and a formal SLA amendment for canary rules.

Hannah/Rishi — we need exec signoff to offer B as it's above standard discretionary thresholds. If no response by EOD we'll offer A as an interim.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Executive escalation: request approval for FinixPay credit above threshold

Hannah/Rishi — quick ask: FinixPay experienced a high-severity outage window that materially exceeded minor SLA tolerances. The customer is pushing for full reimbursement (option B). Finance/legal thresholds require exec approval for credits > $5k.

Recommendation: approve option B (full failed-call reimbursement ~$9k) conditional on:
- We deliver a signed canary agreement (90 days) and a scheduled patch release with pre-production canaries executed and monitored;
- A documented postmortem and mitigation plan be shared within 72 hours.

Approving will preserve the customer (payments vendor) and avoid an escalation to their CISO/GC. If you prefer, offer option A immediately as a short-term goodwill credit and continue negotiation.

—Sean
